problems.problem: Critic-2's problem on this entry still stands, because its revision was refuted only on the plain clause and the original went back into the batch unchanged. (1) The spread is still off. Yāska treats this key verse in Nirukta 5.25, which is in the day's own packet and which Sāyaṇa himself cites. The two readings genuinely differ: Sāyaṇa takes only debt and adds evildoing and the lack of Indra's grace, while Yāska gives 'remained here, i.e. in this very place, or in debt, or in this world'. Sāyaṇa still holds 29 of 30 days and the gate warns about it. This is the one day in the batch where Yāska has a real comment on the key line: on 10.121.1 (Nirukta 10.23) and 10.151.1 (Nirukta 9.31) he only restates or etymologises. (2) This is an exclusion passage (the verdict marks it sensitivity: exclusion), and 'the singer turns to the fate of others' does not state it in the one plain clause that rule 6 asks for.
problems.fix: Use the two-commentator form with a context clause taken from the hymn itself, as the refuter suggested. This version passes entry-check.js (scratch/critic3-110.json, under the 60-word cap, with no four-word run from the key verse): 'Between bidding Indra sit on the holy grass and wishing the evil-hearted far away, the singer sets two fates at the sacrifice side by side; Sāyaṇa, on 10.44.6, reads those left behind as evildoers without Indra’s grace, brought low by debt, and Yāska, Nirukta 5.25, as those who stayed in this very world, or in debt.' Add by2 yaska, and keep the revise file's src and evidence (sa.wikisource revision 328215 and Sarup's Nirukta 5.25, both via packet).
